hero_h1: Rainy Asakusa — Where to Go When It Rains
hero_lead: Tokyo's rainy season hits in June, but Asakusa is actually one of the best parts of the city when it pours. Covered arcades, museums, indoor markets, and tucked-away cafés — here's how to stay dry and still see real Tokyo, all within 15 minutes of Komei Hotel.
schema_headline: Rainy Asakusa — Indoor Guide for Rainy Days in Tokyo

sections.heading: Nakamise Shopping Street — Covered, Crowded, Worth It

blocks.text: The 250-meter arcade from Kaminarimon to the main hall of Senso-ji is fully covered. Even in the heaviest downpour you stay dry, browsing 90+ stalls selling sweets, fans, kimono accessories, and souvenirs. It gets crowded — but rain thins the international tour-bus traffic considerably. A surprisingly pleasant time to visit.

items: Kaminari Okoshi — crunchy rice puff sweets, easy to share, lasts in your bag
Ningyo-yaki — small custard cakes shaped like the Asakusa pagoda. Best eaten warm.
Asakusa Menchi — minced beef croquette, ¥400, eat it under the eaves
Soft-serve at Asakusa Silk Pudding — only ¥350, sit by the window and watch rain on the lanterns

blocks.text: If you only do one indoor activity in Sumida, make it this. The Edo-Tokyo Museum (in Ryogoku, just south of Komei Hotel) is one of Tokyo's best museums — life-size recreations of Edo period streets, an entire Kabuki theatre interior, and beautifully designed English-language displays. Allow 2-3 hours.

Tokyo Skytree Town is the other classic rainy-day pivot. Underground from Oshiage Station, you can spend half a day in the connected shopping mall, aquarium (Sumida Aquarium), and planetarium without ever stepping outside.

sections.heading: Kuramae Cafés — The Rainy-Day Sweet Spot

blocks.text: Kuramae's slow-paced café scene was made for rainy afternoons. Most cafés are in converted warehouses and old shophouses — cozy, candlelit, perfect for working from a laptop while watching the rain pelt the small windows.

items: From Afar Tokyo — antique shop / café in a 100-year-old kura. Order the seasonal pour-over and a chiffon cake.
Dandelion Chocolate Kuramae — bean-to-bar in a warehouse. The hot chocolate is a rainy-day religion.
Coffee Wrights Kuramae — minimalist roaster, big windows, hot milk + filter coffee.
Bridge Coffee & Icecream — riverside espresso, 3 min from Komei. Surprisingly nice from inside when the river is misty.

blocks.text: If browsing isn't your thing, the neighborhood has surprisingly good hands-on workshops. All advance booking required.

items: Kakimori (Kuramae) — make your own notebook with a custom leather cover and dip-pen-friendly paper. About ¥3,000, 45 minutes.
Ganko Kappabashi — make a plastic food sample (sampuru). Tempura is the easiest first project; about ¥2,500.
Asakusa Cooking Studio — sushi or ramen classes with English-speaking instructors. ¥6,000-¥8,000, 2 hours.

blocks.text: This is the underrated rainy-day option for guests staying at Komei Hotel. The whole house is yours: two floors, full kitchen, Netflix, a deep soaking tub, and the covered rooftop terrace (yes, you can sit on the roof in a light rain — it's beautiful).
Pro tip: The 2F living room has a north-facing window that frames the Skytree perfectly during a passing storm. Bring tea, watch the lightning. Some of the best Tokyo memories are made indoors.
Where to buy a cheap umbrella

Any 7-Eleven, Family Mart, or Lawson sells clear plastic umbrellas for ¥500-¥800. Don Quijote has fancier ones. Don't bother bringing a travel umbrella — the Japanese clear one becomes a fun souvenir.
Komei Hotel has a clothes dryer plus the dehumidifier — leave wet jackets and shoes by the entrance and they'll be ready by morning.
Tokyo trains are largely unaffected by rain. Heavy storms (台風 / typhoons) in late June can delay JR lines; the subway lines (Toei Asakusa, Ginza) almost always run.

cta_h2: Rain or shine, the house is yours.
cta_lead: Komei Hotel has a kitchen, a soaking tub, a rooftop with a view, and a dehumidifier. Sometimes the best Tokyo days are spent indoors. Book direct — save up to 10% vs Airbnb.
